headline: A Reading Of 'Dinner With Monoliths' By Joseph Lamour
lede:
In my dating life, I have a few moments that stand out to me. When I was 20, I literally kissed a guy in the summer when it started to rain on our first date. (I mean, you couldn't ask for a more Romantic Comedy starring YOU kind of moment, am I right?) When I was a junior in art college, I had my first serious boyfriend. So serious, that we met each other's parents over Christmas break. I met his in Brooklyn, and then the next week, over Christmas, he met mine in Washington DC.

The following poem I wrote after the experience of having him stay over my parents house. They're Haitian, very religious and quite homophobic, still — unfortunately. They love me, but the "being-gay-is-bad" mantra was driven into them when they were young and now they're elderly (both in their 70s).

I'm still pulling for 'em.

From a guy who's been on the receiving end of years of low-grade hate from family members (not all of them!), maybe think about how it feels to be on the other side of your discomfort with someone's life. And ask yourself why you feel so uncomfortable, maybe.

headline: The Truth About The Ferguson Case That Most People Won't Acknowledge
lede:
Some things I have learned:

Pro Publica recently did an in-depth analysis and found that black kids between the ages of 15-19 are 21 times more likely to be shot and killed by cops than white kids of the same age. That's an insane statistic. That's per capita, not actual numbers. If you are a black teenage boy, you have a 21x higher risk of being shot by police.

Also, in 2010, Federal prosecutors took 162,000 cases to a grand jury. You know how many DIDN'T go to trial? 6.

Also, Mike Brown's family will never get a state criminal trial to get justice for their son. And the testimony that denied them that right technically doesn't make any sense. Seriously, go read it.

headline: Sorry, Toymakers Mass-Producing Warped Body Image, He's Got A Paintbrush And He Knows How To Use It
lede:
I have a very easy confession to make. I grew up with Barbie, and I loved braiding her hair.

She never factored into any storytelling I did (that was reserved for my music videos I directed using a camcorder and my sister and her friends — you should see my interpretation Weezer's 'Sweater Song' — a lot of sweaters were involved), but in the 90s, Barbie had super a cool minidresses and super long hair and I lovvvvved that about her.

She looked like this:

and she was ev-a-reee-thaaang.

I *still* want to be that Barbie, honestly.

So as much as I do love Barbie as a child of the 90s, seeing artist Noel Cruz flip the script on mass produced beauty ideals. He takes the face of, in this case, the Hunger Games Katniss Barbie,

If this doesn't point out the pointlessness of paying attention to the way large corporations view women (profiteers who don't think it's worth the time to make female (and male) look like THEMSELVES when there's money to be made) — I don't know what does.

Yeah, not every kid's gonna get a handpainted real-face Barbie. But every kid might see this and go — wait. There's value in looking real. And *that* is ev-a-ree-THANG.

headline: 16 Years Ago, A Doctor Published A Study. It Was Completely Made Up, And It Made Us All Sicker.
lede:
Once upon a time, a scientist named Dr. Andrew Wakefield published in the medical journal The Lancet that he had discovered a link between autism and vaccines. After years of controversy and making parents mistrust vaccines, along with collecting $674,000 from lawyers who would benefit from suing vaccine makers, it was discovered he had made the whole thing up. The Lancet publicly apologized and reported that further investigation led to the discovery that he had fabricated everything.

In the intervening years, millions have been spent on studying this further to see if there was anything that could connect autism and vaccines. This is what they found.
share_text: The mind reels.

headline: 16 Years Ago, A Doctor Published A Study. It Was Completely Made Up, And It Made Us All Sicker.
lede:
Once upon a time, a scientist named Dr. Andrew Wakefield published in the medical journal The Lancet that he had discovered a link between autism and vaccines. After years of controversy and making parents mistrust vaccines, along with collecting $674,000 from lawyers who would benefit from suing vaccine makers, it was discovered he had made the whole thing up. The Lancet publicly apologized and reported that further investigation led to the discovery that he had fabricated everything.

In the intervening years, millions have been spent on studying this further to see if there was anything that could connect autism and vaccines. This is what they found.

And as a part of that work, she is involved with the community of advocates and activists who help change laws and attitudes toward sexual abuse in real life.

headline: We All Love To Get Our Packages In A Hurry. Here's The Dirty Secret Behind How They Do That.
lede:
Listen, I really don't want to be that guy. I, too, love receiving my packages promptly and am no stranger to the giddy sensation of seeing that cardboard box waiting for me at my doorstep.

But everything has its costs, and to make this modern luxury a reality, companies like Amazon, WalMart, and others are creating an entire sector of low-paid, under-protected temporary workers who are routinely boxing and shipping items they couldn't afford to buy. Here's an inside look at how it's changing the American economy and degrading working conditions for everyone.

headline: Here's A Piece Of History That You Can Help Save Today
lede:
During World War II, women entered the blue collar workforce in huge numbers all over the country. One such place was the Willow Run factory in Michigan where the woman who eventually became “Rosie The Riveter” worked.

That factory us about to be torn down, but there’s a group of people working frantically to try to purchase a small part of the plant and turn it into a museum. They’ve raised 85% of what they need, but with just one day left, there’s a chance they won’t get there. Check the video out and then below that, I’ll tell you how you can help.

headline: Here's How One Cook Is Transforming How People On Food Stamps Eat Dinner
lede: The Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, better known as SNAP or food stamps, helps low and no income people in the US purchase food. Sounds awesome right? Just thinking of all the people who are going to benefit from this book, makes me love the project even more.

headline: The Reply This Star Gives To A "Gay Stereotype" Question Is Brilliant
lede:
As a gay who dates online, I often come across the term "straight-acting" in reference to what the guy I'm looking at wants in a partner, or how he acts himself. What that term implies, to me at least, is "acceptable to be seen with". In my opinion, that's pretty twisted thinking.

Jordan Gavaris plays fellow shiny shoe owner Felix Dawkins in "Orphan Black", one of the more "stereotypically gay" characters on TV today. I can only imagine Jordan gets asked this question about Felix all the time, but what a great answer he gives.

lede: So, Chevron’s using this law called the Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations (RICO) Act to try to stop people from speaking up about pollution in the Ecuadorian Amazon. If Chevron gets away with this, well, it could mean something all of us should worry about.

So Ashley did what any mum would so and as she was purchasing $150 worth of items from the store, she asked if she could use one of the empty dressing rooms to feed him. They refused and were all like this.

But lo and behold, here is Saturday Night Live to hilariously convey the sheer ?!?!?!? of this moment.

lede:

What?

OK, just watch Kelly McGonigal. She says it much better than I do. At 2:24 people just have to laugh, because what she's telling us makes us sound a little bonkers. headline: Every Person On Earth Is Supposed To Have These. But What Are They Exactly?
lede:
There are a lot of terms we throw around, but maybe we've forgotten the true meanings. If all you know about human rights is that a lot of people put those "=" bumper stickers on their cars, or make them their Facebook picture, you could probably use a refresher course.

And if your refresher course comes from 25+ brilliant minds who work hard to uphold our human rights? Bonus.

I especially appreciate what they say starting at 2:40 - just who are the people we need protecting from? And at 3:06 I feel encouraged to keep speaking up on social media platforms (I hope you do, too). At 4:12, a quick, eye-opening story about how it feels to be denied your human rights is all the reminder we should need to keep working on these issues.

We used to be a country that had a social compact that if you worked hard your whole life, you could build a decent savings, buy a house, retire with a great pension and healthcare, your kids could go to school and then get a great job and you didn’t have to worry about them living with you forever for lack of decent jobs. Here’s Robert Reich with some hints about how that came to be.

headline: Billie Holiday With One Of The Most Powerful And Emotional Performances Ever Captured On Video
lede:
Though it was originally written by someone else as a protest song of sorts, this is one of those gems that a singer just takes and totally owns from the start. “Strange Fruit” was shocking to many people when it came out originally in 1939. Even Ms. Holiday herself was initially reluctant to sing it, fearing retribution. Though many people knew that lynchings of African Americans in the South were relatively common, there was much resistance to ending it, since it was a very effective means of social control and political intimidation by Southern whites.

Because the song was so powerful and poignant for Holiday, there were some rules when she performed it: she would close the evening with the song, the waiters would stop service when the song began, and the room would be in total darkness except for a spotlight on Billie Holiday’s face. And there would be no encore.

Her voice is strong and impressive in this clip, but just look at the incredible expressiveness in her eyes as she gets through the haunting lyrics.

Trigger warning: lyrics about racial violence.

headline: See Putin's Homophobic Spokesman Gets Shamed On 'The Daily Show.' And That's The Least Awesome Part.
lede:
In the run up to the Sochi Olympics, there was uproar over Russia's awful anti-gay laws that were destroying lives and families. The Daily Show decided to head over to find out what the deal was and interviewed one of Putin's spokesmen. Said spokesman confirmed all their worst fears. So Jason Jones went onto the streets to find out more. And although he discovered 74% of Russians are anti-gay, he also found pockets of beautiful dissent. At 4:06, he asks the people that really matter, a bunch of LGBTQ Russians, why they don't just leave. At 5:40, he meets an amazing woman who actually makes me tear up a little. It doesn't even end with a joke.

If you live somewhere other than the USA, I've provided instructions on how to see the video at the bottom of the page. Because you deserve better than a media company's awful region restrictions.

headline: The Answer To The Fashion Industry’s Environmental Crisis? Milk It For All It's Worth.
lede:
It can be pretty easy to forget what the garment industry does to the environment. From field to factory to laundry to landfill, our clothes are taking a huge toll on the planet at every stage of their lives.

But all hope is not lost! Inventors like the woman in this video have been coming up with eco-friendly alternatives to conventional materials that are produced consciously with little to no waste. The more of these we’ve got around, the better off we’ll all be. And, when they look like this, our wardrobes won’t suffer either!

headline: The 14 Stunning Photographs Of Couples In Love
lede:
When you think of iconic romance, what image do you get? The chances are you think of a man and woman in films, music videos and television shows where their portrayals of love are often of straight white couples.

Photographer Branden Summers could only think of straight couples when he thought of iconic romance, and so he decided to help change that lack of representation by photographing gay couples from around the world embracing their love. Branden wanted to show that love was equal worldwide, and said, "My hope is that not only are my images inspiring romance for the queer community, but inspiring the acceptance of our romance on a global scale."

I really recommend watching the video before you look at the stunning photos, as it really helps add context to the project.

There's always a lot of chitter chatter on the Upworthy Facebook page, and we read every comment you post. For real: the good, the bad, and even the four paragraph replies.

At the start of 2014, we asked you what you got up to at the end of last year, and eeeeesh I did not expect to read such lovely answers. If you've ever wondered who the people are that you comment alongside on our page, here's a little glimpse into their lives and what they do to make the world a little better for all of us.

You all make me feel like this.

headline: They Worked On It For 9 Long Years. Now's Your Chance To See It In Person.
lede:
A few months ago, we posted about a fundraiser for the Beehive Design Collective. What's the Beehive Design Collective, you ask? It's a group of amazing artists that creates story graphics on themes of globalization and resistance. Their work is fantastically detailed and chock-full of both history and passion.

The Bees' most recent poster (the subject of their fundraising campaign) is called Mesoamérica Resiste. It tells stories of resistance, resilience, and solidarity from Mexico to Colombia. It shows the modern invasion of megaprojects planned for the region as well as grassroots efforts to defend land and traditions, protect cultural and ecological diversity, and build alternative economies.

So whatever happened with that campaign? Well, in large part thanks to Upworthians like you donating and sharing the post, the Bees more than tripled their fundraising and outreach goals, ending up just a few dollars short of a whopping $118,000 from 3,000 backers around the world.

But the story's not over! You can learn about the next chapter of the Bee's adventure once the poster went to print and watch the video below.

headline: A Man Slams A Bigoted Question Down So Hard He Brings Down The House
lede:
Oftentimes, people of color are asked, "What kind of ____ are you?" in relation to their ethnicity. It's quite a different question than "Where are you from?" if you think about it. A Korean-American person may be asked which country in Asia they may be from, or they could be asked, "What kind of Asian are you?"

Doesn't that kind of sound like someone is asking what brand they are? It does to me. Even if it doesn't to you, it's quite a loaded question — one that Alex Dang is ponders below.

headline: A Compilation Of The Most Common (Terrible) Advice For Avoiding Rape
lede:
Okay, let's give college bulletins and the glossy magazines the benefit of the doubt: maybe they're seriously concerned with stopping rapes on campuses (and elsewhere). And maybe they sincerely believe that a good way to do that is to suggest some of the steps you'll see below.

The problem is that when you focus on controlling how women behave to avoid rape, however well-meaning that advice is, you're missing a pretty big piece of the reason why rape is so prevalent. Namely, rapists. I'd much rather see a discussion about how we get men to understand consent and stop being creepers than the bizarre, contradictory wardrobe suggestions brilliantly parodied in this video.

headline: Stop Telling Women To Smile
lede:
Every day women are harassed in the street simply by being a woman. Or in other words: every time we step out the house we run the risk of being shouted at, cat-called or assaulted usually in broad daylight. FUN!

Brooklyn based artist Tatyana Fazlalizadeh wanted to take women's voices and faces and plaster them big and bold in the very same places where this takes place. She's addressing gender based street harassment by taking a place where women feel uncomfortable and turning it into a place where we cannot be ignored through street art, and that is pretty awesome.

headline: Barbie? Please. A New Doll for Kids Resembles Actual Humans. (Bonus: She Doesn't Walk On Her Toes.)
lede:

We thought it would be pretty cool if toy makers took notice and started creating dolls for our kids that are more realistic.

Well, that hasn't happened, so Nickolay decided to make his own "average" dolls. He's running a crowdfunding project, and you can help support it by donating or ordering a doll.

headline: Just When A Problem Like Child Slavery Seems So Big We Don't Know What To Do, A 9-Year-Old Shows Us
lede:

headline: Hear What These Celebrities Have To Say About The 'Ban Bossy' Campaign
lede:
I read a lot of "banning words is stupid!" type of comments flood my Facebook and Twitter feed when the #BanBossy campaign was launched by Lean In. But here's the deal: the focus should be on the bigger statement being made, and that is how many are using language and words like "bossy" in a derogatory way towards young girls who are simply asserting themselves. It may seem like a small issue to some, but the campaign is speaking to the young girls sitting in classrooms right now who are afraid to speak out, not to the cynical internet commenters.

So to the young girls online reading this: Beyoncé, Condoleezza Rice & Jane Lynch have your back if you wana go ahead and speak up.

headline: I Never Knew A Happy Meal Could Make Me This Sad
lede:
It can be tough to get kids to eat right. But developing healthy eating habits is an important lesson to pass on--after all, most kids would happily eat chocolate ice cream three times a day if we let them. A fast food kid’s meal probably seems like a nutritious option, but as this video demonstrates, those fast food companies still give kids more food than most of them need in a single meal.

While not every child will love the alternative recipe provided in the video, there are still plenty of other ways to make dinnertime healthier for your kids. If a home-cooked meal isn’t feasible every night, opting for the healthiest food on the restaurant menu and encouraging kids to stop eating when they’re full, rather than pushing them to clean their plates, can make a positive difference here.

headline: Why Talking To Babies Is An Investment Worth Making. Don't Believe Me? Watch And Learn.
lede: Did you know that the learning process for kids starts way before kindergarten? And before pre-school too? Babies are actually learning all the time, so how we talk to them is really important, because it is literally helping their brains grow! Unfortunately, kids born in poverty often do not get the interaction needed to promote that kind of brain growth, and as a result end up hearing on average 30 million fewer words in their earliest years compared to kids born into wealthier families. It's a real shame that something so far beyond their control puts these kids at a disadvantage before they even put on their first-day-of-school outfit. Here's a look at the science behind it and how we can help all of our little ones succeed!

headline: Who Wants To Learn Some Eye-Opening And Disturbing Things About Elephants?
lede:
Elephants are the only mammal aside from humans to have something approximating a funeral when their family member dies. They try to heal them, they comfort them, then they often have a rudimentary burial. Which brings me to the important part.

So there's this site called Quora.com. A lot of people write there, myself included. A few of the writers there got together and decided to help a fellow Quoran and ranger in Zambia, Rory Young, in his efforts to prevent the extinction of African Elephants. They could become extinct within 6 years if action isn't taken. So learn more about what they're doing, and if you are up for it, spread the word and help.

headline: You Marry The Love Of Your Life. Then The Feds Get An Address Wrong And Arrest Them?
lede: Emily fell in love with a man named Pedro. They got married and had an adorable little kid. Pedro had come to the states when he was 8. His family was here legally and seeking permanent residency. His mother had memory problems, made an error in her hearing, and was denied permanent residency. The feds still had a work visa for Pedro, and sent it to an old address (despite having sent previous visas to his current one.) When he didn't respond, they decided to deport him. Even though they sent it to the wrong address. And that is where our story begins...

headline: In Case You Missed It: New Pope Got All Muslim-y During A Serious Christian Holy Week
lede:
Quick breakdown on what's historic about this, folks:

1) All Popes have washed and kissed feet in this Maundy Thursday ceremony, which is a remembrance of the Last Supper Jesus shared with His disciples. No Pope ever has included women. This Pope just included TWO. (This is supposedly because Jesus' disciples were all men, although I'd love to hear what Mary Magdalene would have to say about that!) 

2) All Popes have performed this ceremony with other Catholic priests. No Pope ever has included Muslims. No Pope ever has included prisoners. 

And then he rounded out the service by telling Christians they should do a lot less navel-gazing ("It is not in soul-searching or constant introspection that we encounter the Lord.”) and a lot more caring for the poor (“We need to go out to the outskirts where there is suffering, bloodshed, blindness that longs for sight, and prisoners in thrall to many evil masters.”)

If you've never experienced a foot-washing ceremony, they are quite moving — symbolizing the humility and service that should characterize leadership in the Christian tradition. Check it out:

headline: Why Voldemort's Mom Could Have Been The Hero Of The Harry Potter Books
lede:
When you reduce a major government decision with serious real world impacts to a flimsy argument about a couple of fictional characters, you better be prepared for those of us who've actually read the books to blow some holes in your fanciful theory. 

1) If Lily Potter had gotten an abortion, Neville Longbottom would have killed Voldemort. The prophecy said so.

2) The whole mess could've been avoided if only Tom Riddle's mother had gotten an abortion in the first place.

Now please, go read the books. You might actually learn something.

So they sang her a lovely song to help inspire her to keep fighting for real immigration reform.

lede:
Community radio stations are a lot like the Internet: they bring groups of people together and help people get information. The difference? You don't need a computer, Internet access, or even to know how to read. That's what makes them so powerful for organizing after disasters and for reaching marginalized communities. 

Check out the pretty fantastic ways community radio has made a huge difference. Then get excited, because the government is about to open the airwaves for a whole lot of new stations to form!

Even if you think you've got nothing to hide, you need to know that your freedom of expression is on the line.

Turns out, there's data that shows something pretty interesting about states that make laws allowing for freeloaders. Whoops, I mean, those who don't wish to pay dues for the good job they get.

How can you tell if a movie doesn't do a sucky job with it's presence of female characters? Well pretty easy really: if it can't answer the three questions that are asked in this video, then it fails the Bechdel Test.

The Bechdel Test was created by Allison Bechdel and it is just a simple way of evaluating if women talk about anything other than men — jobs, friendships, politics, life... seriously, anything else.

Oh, and the list of films she shows below is also deeeeeppressssssssingly long.

headline: Awww, SNAP! — One Congressman Tries Living On Food Stamps
lede:
While the threat to cutbacks in food stamps died with the recent farm bill, it will most certainly be back on the agenda shortly. Now called the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), my family lived on them at times when growing up in the Midwest. I'll save you the story, but if not for that and a few other 1970s food supplement programs, we would have starved — no question in my mind. As it was, we could only afford cheap, high-sugar, not very nutritious items with the amount my mother received.

Watch this Congressman face the same choices as his grocery budget gets real tight when he tries to live on the amount that his fellow elected officials want folks to live on.

headline: Its Not A Hymn For Hoodies. Its A Vivid Reminder Of The Biggest Question About This Whole Mess.
lede:
Before things got cloudy in the killing of Trayvon Martin trial, we have to go back to that window of time between his death and when there had not even been an arrest made. Why had that taken so long? What was the delay? Thats what I remember asking. The reasons for that oh-too-long pause, exemplified through this song, gives us a peaceful reminder of how hard it was to get justice in motion and now, how much further justice has to go.

The line that really gets to me comes at 3:25 because it calls attention to such a simple fact, and yet it became so much more than that.

headline: I Don’t Think Eminem Realizes He’s Become A Science Teacher
lede:
Nas, Tupac, Common, Public Enemy … these rappers taught this white British girl living in a small village about the ways of world. No really, I learnt (and sang along to) every word to Lauryn Hill's Miseducation album at the age of 13. I still do.

Embarrassing confessions aside, this is why I was so happy to see this incredibly innovative teaching method: combine something you love (rap) with something valuable (education) and look at how the kids faces light up with joy when they realize that real learning isn't just text books, whiteboards and tests.

This dreamboat is starting a country career out of the closet, and he's singing his truth.

headline: The Fact That I Thought These Awful Reality TV Ads Were Real Should Scare Us
lede: I get a little depressed each time great public television like NOVA or Frontline or the Newshour are threatened with funding cuts when shows like the Real House Cats of Chattanooga or Survivor 34: Upstate New York or So You Think You Can Twerk are owning the airwaves. So you can imagine my utter joy when one public broadcasting station decided to openly mock reality TV by producing fake ads so bad they could actually be real shows. If we don't support public television, I'm really afraid the former might become the latter.

lede: Jim Gaffigan's 2004 standup special "Beyond the Pale" contains some hilarious jokes on the well-traveled subject of overeating and the devastating lack of health and nutrition in America. To really drive the point home, he invented a fictional and absurdly unhealthy "doughnut ham hamburger." Nine years later, Gaffigan's joke became reality. If this isn't the wakeup call for America to make a big ol' cultural U-turn in the name of health, I don't know what is.

To really drive the point home, he invented a fictional and absurdly unhealthy "doughnut ham hamburger." Nine years later, Gaffigan's joke became reality. If this isn't the wakeup call for America to make a big ol' cultural U-turn in the name of health, I don't know what is.

headline: The Fact That These Ads Are Fake Is Hilarious. That Everyone Thought They Are Real Is Disconcerting.

If we don't support public television, I'm really afraid the former might become the latter.

headline: WATCH: The Most Honest Lady-Business Advertisement I've Ever Seen. Period.
lede: FINALLY! An ad that normalizes talking about periods for a younger crowd. Getting your period is SO not something to be embarrassed about, but you'd never guess that from the way most tampon and pad ads go out of their way to not talk about what their products are used for. I'm really glad this ad doesn't try to cover up what a period is with poetic language, nondescript neon-blue liquid demonstrations, or slow-mo shots of girls dancing on beaches in white pants. Periods are normal. Talking about them and how to handle them should be normal, too.

headline: Why 'This Land Is Your Land' Was A Pretty Provocative Song
lede:
Did you know that the last part of the old Woody Guthrie favorite, "This Land Is Your Land," is usually left off of printed versions of the song, because some deemed it a bit too ... edgy for schoolkids? To me, the lyrics are quite wonderful, and spot-on for our hard times:

In the shadow of the steeple I saw my people,
By the relief office I seen my people;
As they stood there hungry, I stood there asking
Is this land made for you and me?

Catch all of the lyrics below the video, which features award-winning Journalist and Commentator Bill Moyers celebrating Woody Guthrie's legacy.

headline: Anything That Gets Marina Abramović Grinding With Jay Z Wins In My Book
lede:
A few years ago art icon Marina Abramović lifted the performance art world to a broader audience with “The Artist Is Present.” I’m simplifying here, but she sat quietly at a table in a white room for a long time. Her audience, one by one, sat across from her and looked her right in the eyes.

Once even Lady Gagashowed up. Soon people who never would have gone to a performance art show were in line.

Well, here we are now with Jay Z putting himself in a similar situation. Look, whatever you think of his lyrics you've got to at least appreciate a hip hop artist who istrying to redefine himself and push rap into new territory. At the very least, I see this video as a gateway drug into different cultures. What do you think, did it work?

headline: 'One Of These Things Is Not Like The Others' Shouldn't Have Come To Mind When I Viewed A Class Photo
lede:
I'm positive that the photographer who took the original photo wasn't an unkind person who intentionally separated a child in his class photo. But the original picture made one little boy who so clearly wanted to be a part of his class look (and maybe feel) like he was alone. And just as bad, it sent a message to his peers that it's okay to exclude children with disabilities.

My original thought was that if all the kids just moved closer, the problem would be solved. But a friend who has a child with a disability helped me to understand that wouldn't have been a solution, either, because he'd still be separated.

Although it took a little pressure, the photography company retook the class picture and the new one is perfect. Let's learn from this mistake. Small adjustments in our daily actions can make everyone feel included, important and valued.

headline: Alright Parents, Let's Just Acknowledge That We're All Doing Our Best Already
lede:
Breastfeed, bottle feed. Homeschool, public school. Stay at home, continue your career. Have a family while you're in your early 20's, wait until you're 40.

If I see one more article criticizing moms for their choices, I might scream. Or weep. Actually, I'll probably just roll my eyes. But how about this: we all agree that we're doing the best we can, no two moms are the same, what we do for our family might not work for another family, and, oh yeah, nobody's "right." Or everybody's "right." Either one.

I want to make the best choices I can for my kids, and I also want to do my best to avoid making other moms feel like they're making bad choices just because they're not the same choices. Who else is in?

lede:
As the gay child of two very religious parents, I've learned that there are two ways I can bring up my love life: 1. The "Vague Pronoun" Method; or 2. the "Mention Anything and Ruin Everyone's Day with the Inevitable Argument That May End in a Slammed Door or a Skipped Holiday" Method. That's no way for a family to remain healthy.

Luckily for us, Stef Foster (Teri Polo) from ABC Family's "The Fosters" knows just what to say to her father (Sam McMurray) who doesn't keep an open dialog with his kid. Share this if you want people to see things from another perspective.

headline: A Message To Everyone Out There Who Thinks They Aren't Beautiful In Pictures
lede:
My best friend doesn't think she takes a good picture. You know that thing that people do when you take a cell phone picture 3 times before it's deemed "acceptable"? That's her. And she is one of the most beautiful people I've met (no, you can't see a picture, because I want to stay friends with her after this gets published.)

The point I'm making is the same one JJ Tiziou is making with his project. When so many people around us think they're somehow not worthy to be immortalized in film, there's a problem. Everyone should be happy to capture the moments in their lives.

headline: Usually Tampon Ads Give Me Cramps And A Headache. This One Makes Me Smile.
lede: FINALLY! An ad that normalizes talking about periods for a younger crowd. Getting your period is SO not something to be embarrassed about, but you'd never guess that from the way most tampon and pad ads go out of their way to not talk about what their products are used for. I'm really glad this ad doesn't try to cover up what a period is with poetic language, nondescript neon-blue liquid demonstrations, or slow-mo shots of girls dancing on beaches in white pants. Periods are normal. Talking about them and how to handle them should be normal, too.

headline: Are You Outraged Because You Think This Couldn't Happen, Or Because You Know It Does Every Day?
lede:
At nearly 1 am on May 16th, 2010, on an unlit street in the East Side of Detroit, a Special Response Team (Detroit Police Department’s version of a SWAT team) raided a duplex in search of a murder suspect. A single shot was fired. It struck and killed Aiyanna Stanley-Jones. She was 7 years old.

There are no easy answers to explain something this horrific. But, at least one of the questions that should be asked is whether the 25-year trend of fighting the War On Drugs by outfitting our police forces with the tools and mentality of an invading army is really worth this type of casualty. If the video below moves you, help immortalize Aiyanna by sharing it.

lede:

But then I came across a little girl called Emilia. Emilia was only 8 years old when she was diagnosed with a deadly lung condition, and watching this I could see that she perfectly captures an inspiring, strong willed and brave nature that so many of us lack. Emilia had a last wish – watch as her mum, Rachel, and a team of kind people make that wish come true.

headline: If You Are Wondering What Costumes NOT To Wear This Halloween, Here Are Some Examples
lede:
When combing the isles of the pop-up Halloween store doing last minute shopping for you or your kids' big Thursday night on the town, a few things to keep in mind:

1. No one likes to be offended on a day of celebration and fun, and 2. Someone else's culture/heritage doesn't qualify as a costume. It has historical significance, and simplifying it into a gag, mockery, or skimpy outfit is just downright disrespectful, and a buzzkill.

The costume of a goblin or a fairy next to it? Perfect. Goblins aren't real, and fairies can be brought back to life with clapping if you offend them to death. Below are some examples of what to skip over as options.

headline: A Marine Was Assaulted. Her Commander Said She Deserved It For Wearing Running Shorts. Really.
lede:

What followed was a horror show where she was intimidated by her superiors, maliciously harassed, and victimized again by the military branch she volunteered to serve in. I can't imagine going through what Ariana went through and remaining sane. There are really easy ways this could all be fixed by simply taking these investigations out of the military chain of command, yet we are still debating wether it's a good idea. At 3:45, her husband explains how lucky he is.

Learn her story. Then make sure people know about it until the Military brass are shamed into doing the right thing.

lede:

— Dean Trippe

lede:
President Kennedy was a transformational leader, and it's hard to imagine what it felt like to hear of his assassination in 1963. When he was shot, the Boston Symphony Orchestra was about to begin its regular Friday afternoon concert. By the time they found out President Kennedy had died, the audience was already seated, oblivious to the world-changing events happening in Dallas.

In a powerful--and stunningly level-headed--decision, the orchestra's Music Director, Erich Leinsdorf, sent librarian William Shisler to get the music for the funeral march from Beethoven's "Eroica" symphony. Shisler quickly distributed the music onstage, letting the musicians know what had happened.

This recording, from WGBH in Boston, begins when Leinsdorf takes the stage to announce the terrible news to the audience and captures the BSO's heart-rending performance of the Beethoven symphony--a work they had found out they were playing only minutes before.

headline: We Don’t Hear Enough From Native American Voices. Here’s An Inspiring Message From One.
lede:
The Oglala Lakota live on Pine Ridge Indian Reservation in South Dakota, near the Black Hills. The area has a pretty tragic history of violence, broken treaties, and culture clashes, beginning in 1874, when prospectors discovered gold in the Black Hills and the the U.S. government seized the land that had previously been guaranteed to the tribe.

Today, what little we hear about the reservation is usually about the poverty, violence, and alcoholism. While that does exist, that is just one story of many. I wish we heard more stories like this, about the beauty of the land and the spirituality and strength of the people.

excerpt: A woman whose people have endured hardship still believes it’s all about peace.

headline: Beautiful Advice On How To Live From Nelson Mandela
lede:
Nelson Mandela was a symbol of courage. After he was released from an unjust 27 year prison stay in 1990, he lead the way for the abolition of apartheid in South Africa in 1994. He was elected as South Africa's first black president that same year. His most astounding accomplishment after suffering years of abuse was to create the Truth and Reconciliation Commission, which focused on healing the country's wounds from human rights abuses using truth-telling and forgiveness.

Mandela later established the Nelson Mandela Foundation to combat poverty and HIV/AIDS.

He passed away on December 5th, 2013. He walked among us as a man for 95 years, but will be remembered as hero as long as there are history books to be read.

Nelson Mandela was a symbol of courage. After he was released from an unjust 27 year prison stay in 1990, he lead the way for the abolition of apartheid in South Africa in 1994. He was elected as South Africa's first black president that same year. His most astounding accomplishment after suffering years of abuse was to create the Truth and Reconciliation Commission, which focused on healing the country's wounds from human rights abuses using truth-telling and forgiveness.

Mandela later established the Nelson Mandela Foundation to combat poverty and HIV/AIDS.

He passed away on December 5th, 2013. He walked among us as a man for 95 years, but will be remembered as hero as long as there are history books to be read.

headline: A Kid Looked Death Right In The Eye And Smiled Warmly. 5000 People Picked Up Where He Left Off.
lede:
Back in May of 2013, my life was changed forever. A fan had written me to let me know that a teenage musician named Zach Sobiech that I had written about earlier in the year had just passed away from a rare cancer. Zach had written a song about coming to terms his imminent death called "Clouds." Cancer is personal to me, you see, as I've lost many people, including my father to it. My mom has hers under control. My son will inevitably have to do something to make sure he doesn't get it. It hit too close to home.

The day Zach passed, I went online to see if I could find any more videos about him to honor his memory, and discovered an amazing documentary short about his brief but beautiful life. I spent a whole day crying, having flashbacks to my father's passing, and made sure it could reach as many people as possible. It was the biggest hit we ever had. 20,000,000 people have seen it. People emailed me from all over the globe to talk about how his story impacted their lives. Parents tweeted me about their lost children. Upworthy readers helped raise $450,000 for the Children's Cancer Fund. His song went on to become the 1st independent artist to reach the top of the iTunes music charts. And I got to know a wonderful team of people who actually knew and loved him.

I'm sad I never got the opportunity to meet him. But 5000 people who did really know him got together to create a giant choir in the middle of Mall of America. Then they sang his song, Clouds, which debuted a year ago. The couple in the middle are his wonderful and supportive and brave parents. And I once again have become a weepy mess.

headline: He Saved 669 Kids Lives From Nazi Death Camps — And What The Audience Does At 0.50 Is Incredible
lede:
Sir Nicholas Winton — who was dubbed the "British Schindler" after saving 669 mostly Jewish children from nazi death camps on the eve of the Second World War – is given the surprise of his life on television and ohhhh my how I did not expect to see the audience do that at 0.50 in.

Winton humbly kept his efforts a secret, until his wife found scrapbooks about saving the children in their attic. The holocaust history should still be very much in the publics mind and our education, and it's little moments like these that should be celebrated and not forgotten.

headline: Is A Moment Of Silence Going To Solve Gun Violence?
lede:
I want to be really clear: I'm not anti-gun. I grew up around guns and I'm still very comfortable handling them. I know many people feel differently and that's okay.

But the point I hope we can all agree on is that something has to change. 35,000 people should not die from gun violence every year. Parents shouldn't ever have to worry that their kids might be shot at school.

We should absolutely observe a moment of silence for terrible tragedies, but we need to remember as part of the bigger picture that silence won't result in change. A majority of Americans, including NRA members, agree that background checks are important. So let's start with universal background checks for private gun sales.

headline: A Kid Looked Death Right In The Eye And Sang This Song. 5000 Friends Picked Up Where He Left Off.
lede:
Back in May of 2013, my life was changed forever. A fan had written me to let me know that a teenage musician named Zach Sobiech that I had written about earlier in the year had just passed away from a rare cancer. Zach had written a song about coming to terms his imminent death called "Clouds." Cancer is personal to me, you see, as I've lost many people, including my father to it. My mom has hers under control. My son will inevitably have to do something to make sure he doesn't get it. It hit too close to home.

The day Zach passed, I went online to see if I could find any more videos about him to honor his memory, and discovered an amazing documentary short about his brief but beautiful life. I spent a whole day crying, having flashbacks to my father's passing, and made sure it could reach as many people as possible. It was the biggest hit we ever had. 20,000,000 people have seen it. People emailed me from all over the globe to talk about how his story impacted their lives. Parents tweeted me about their lost children. Upworthy readers helped raise $450,000 for the Children's Cancer Fund. His song went on to become the 1st independent artist to reach the top of the iTunes music charts. And I got to know a wonderful team of people who actually knew and loved him.

I'm sad I never got the opportunity to meet him. But 5000 people who did really know him got together to create a giant choir in the middle of Mall of America. Then they sang his song, Clouds, which debuted a year ago. The couple in the middle are his wonderful and supportive and brave parents. And I once again have become a weepy mess.

headline: Psychologist Says A Rich Kid Isn't Guilty Because He's Rich. Anderson Says What We're ALL Thinking.
lede:
This whole affluenza thing has thrown us all for a loop. For those who don't know, 16 year-old Ethan Couch was sentenced to 10 years probation after driving drunk, killing 4 and injuring 9. The excuse? A psychologist (being questioned by Anderson below) said he suffered from affluenza: being a rich kid and thus, as a young person of wealth, having no consequences in life and not realising the severity of your actions.

Sure, psychologists the world over have said sentencing in this case is not atypical, but the reasoning behind it is something that we as a people need to put up for examination. The whole situation is pretty absurd.

headline: See These Two Singers Do An Amazing Cover Of Beyonce's Song About The Dangerous Standards Of Beauty
lede:
(Queen) Beyonce recently released a new album, and there was one song that made us here at Upworthy get all excited: 'Pretty Hurts'. The song struck a chord with a lot of people because it has powerful lyrics that explore the damaging ways in which we define beauty, and how the constant strive for perfection is a dangerous "disease of a nation."

Instead of including Beyonce's own awesome video here (y'all need to go and download her album to see that) I came across this wonderful cover by two young singers, Chloe and Halle Bailey, who are crazy talented and perfectly capture the emotion and the core of what the message of the song is all about.

First we had TLC's 'Unpretty' and now we have 'Pretty Hurts' as the anthem for all of us who have ever felt under pressure to fit into a mould we just. don't. fit. in. Now break it down and sing it with me: Preeeeeeettttttyyyyy, huuuuuuurttttssssss.

headline: We're Told That All Humans Are Created Equal. Do You See That In These Photos?
lede:
Humans, we're a funny bunch. We're quick to and pit people against each other in tribes: Liberal vs Conservative, Poor vs Rich, Old vs Young. But we seem to often overlook the fact that despite these seemingly obvious differences, we all still have the fundamental sameness.

That's what fascinated photographer Mark Laita, who decided to stand people of different backgrounds, occupations and appearances next to each other to, in his words, "let the viewer think for themselves about how the two individuals in the photographs relate and what that means."

headline: And Lo, A Snarky YouTube Personality Looked Down On Misogynists And Said, 'Yo, Stop That'
lede:
Ever hear someone point out something sexist about a movie and immediately get the response: "It's just a movie. Get over it"? ... Yeah, me too.

Well, breaking news, y'all: You can like something AND acknowledge that it has faults! No, that doesn't make you a bad fan! In fact, I'd argue that makes you a really, really good fan because you're challenging your favorite thing to DO BETTER — to stop relying on problematic tropes and actually try to create something new, fresh, and fun without marginalizing already marginalized groups. I mean, after all, what are we saying about our culture if we're not actively thinking about the media we consume?

And that's what happens here: The video starts at 2:02 because we get a great summary of the situation at hand without hearing a bunch of Internet trolls being the worst (as always). At 3:41, some dudes try to burn down a woman's career because she pointed out some kinda messed up things about their favorite video game. Definitely stick around to 4:07 for the best response about the media we consume and, you know, actually thinking critically about it.

headline: Let's Learn Some Eye-Opening And Disturbing Things About Elephants
lede:
Elephants are the only mammal aside from humans to have something approximating a funeral when their family member dies. They try to heal them, they comfort them, then they often have a rudimentary burial. Which brings me to the important part.

So there's this site called Quora.com. A lot of people write there, myself included. A few of the writers there got together and decided to help a fellow Quoran and ranger in Zambia, Rory Young, in his efforts to prevent the extinction of African Elephants. They could become extinct within 6 years if action isn't taken. So learn more about what they're doing, and if you are up for it, spread the word and help.

headline: There's An Achievement Gap In America, And It Starts Way Earlier Than Expected
lede: Did you know that the learning process for kids starts way before kindergarten? And before pre-school too? Babies are actually learning all the time, so how we talk to them is really important, because it is literally helping their brains grow! Unfortunately, kids born in poverty often do not get the interaction needed to promote that kind of brain growth, and as a result end up hearing on average 30 million fewer words in their earliest years compared to kids born into wealthier families. It's a real shame that something so far beyond their control puts these kids at a disadvantage before they even put on their first-day-of-school outfit. Here's a look at the science behind it and how we can help all of our little ones succeed!

headline: Banksy Has Updated His Famous 'The Girl With The Balloon' Artwork To Stand With Syria
lede:
The Syria crisis hasn't slowed down, and over 100,000 people have died in three years, with thousands of Syrian's displaced, many of whom are women and children.

But many people are still standing with Syria, including the street artist Banksy who has re-worked his famous and popular art work of a girl reaching for a red balloon with the intention of shedding light on the Syrian crisis. The original artwork depicted a young girl with flowing hair with a heart shaped balloon just beyond her grasp — the new re-working of his classic stencil is of a young Syrian girl accompanied with a #WithSyria hashtag, which is part of a global vigil campaign today to mark the three years since the crisis began.

Have a look at the following below:

1. Banky's original artwork alongside Banksy's new re-worked image, and his website message in support of #WithSyria

2. Photographs of young Syrian children holding red balloons as part of the #WithSyria campaign

3. A photograph of actor Idris Elba with a red balloon supporting the campaign

4. The animated campaign video for #WithSyria with Idrsi Elba narrating and music by the band Elbow

headline: Here Are Some Posters For The Men Who Tell Women What They Think They Should Do In The Street
lede:
Every day women are harassed in the street simply by being a woman. Or in other words: every time we step out the house we run the risk of being shouted at, cat-called or assaulted usually in broad daylight. FUN!

Brooklyn based artist Tatyana Fazlalizadeh wanted to take women's voices and faces and plaster them big and bold in the very same places where this takes place. She's addressing gender based street harassment by taking a place where women feel uncomfortable and turning it into a place where we cannot be ignored through street art, and that is pretty awesome.

headline: A Compilation Of The Most Common (Terrible) Advice For Avoiding Rape
lede:
Okay, let's give college bulletins and the glossy magazines the benefit of the doubt: maybe they're seriously concerned with stopping rapes on campuses (and elsewhere). And maybe they sincerely believe that a good way to do that is to suggest some of the steps you'll see below.

The problem is that when you focus on controlling how women behave to avoid rape, however well-meaning that advice is, you're missing a pretty big piece of the reason why rape is so prevalent. Namely, rapists. I'd much rather see a discussion about how we get men to understand consent and stop being creepers than the bizarre, contradictory wardrobe suggestions brilliantly parodied in this video.

TRIGGER WARNING: Nothing graphic, but this video features fictionalized rape scenarios and at least one incredibly skeevy looking dude.

headline: The 14 Stunning Photographs Of Couples In Love
lede:
When you think of iconic romance, what image do you get? The chances are you think of a man and woman in films, music videos and television shows where their portrayals of love are often of straight white couples.

Photographer Branden Summers could only think of straight couples when he thought of iconic romance, and so he decided to help change that lack of representation by photographing gay couples from around the world embracing their love. Branden wanted to show that love was equal worldwide, and said, "My hope is that not only are my images inspiring romance for the queer community, but inspiring the acceptance of our romance on a global scale."

I really recommend watching the video before you look at the stunning photos, as it really helps add context to the project.

headline: A Series Of Portraits And Feet Somehow Capture The Essence Of The Egytpian Revolution
lede:
I love when art is used as a tool to communicate, and so when exiled Iranian visual artist Shirin Neshat decided to dedicate her new project to the Egyptian Revolution, she wanted to "investigate the universal experience of pain and mourning on both a personal and national level." And wow did she — below is a series of stunning black and white photographs that she hoped would compel the viewer to "acknowledge the toll of political and social upheaval that results when people deny humanity to those whom they perceive as the 'other.'"

What's so amazing is how she captured a feeling of intensity and deep pain in the images by asking her Egyptian subjects to share their stories of tragedy before the camera, capturing a poignant connection between the subject and viewer.

excerpt: Adorable kiddos honor the greats that have come before them.
headline: These Kids Were Asked To Act Like A Famous Idol, And They Knocked It Out Of The Park
lede:
Eunique J. Gibson started the "Because of Them We Can" project in 2013 to honor African Americans who have been pioneers in their fields and to help children see all the possibilities that lie ahead of them. She does it in the coolest, cutest way -- by dressing kids up to emulate these trailblazers and photographing them.

I'll use Ms. Gibson's own words from another video to describe it: "It's about empowering these kids and injecting this new wave of self-esteem and self-worth by understanding what's already been done, what's being done, and what can be done."

It's been wildly popular, which means she's gonna keep expanding on the project, like making videos similar to the one here. I'm happily joining the growing list of people who are super excited to see what else she does next.

headline: A Drag Queen Talks About Homophobia, Ignites A National Debate, Then Beautifully Sums It All Up
lede: This speech, given by Rory O'Neill dressed as Panti Noble, is incredibly poignant and moving. lede:

We're all pretty much in it together in that we wanna live safe and healthy (and awesome) lives. But this is some big-time evidence that a certain approach to that goal is actually doing the opposite.

headline: How The "Trust Us, Let Us Help You" Type Of Development Is Wrong
lede:

Cue this smart, satirical look at how the "trust us, we know best, let us help you" approach that so often comes with development and how it can do more harm than good. Tribal people in our world are having their land robbed, and self-sufficiency and pride destroyed — hear more about how that is happening below.

headline: Something Absolutely Terrible Just Happened To The Internet. Here's Why.
lede:
2014 is shaping up to be a terrible year for the free and open Internet. A Federal court struck down the Net Neutrality rules that prevent charming companies like Comcast and Time Warner Cable from playing favorites with website speeds. For example: Let's say Comcast's cabe division gets tired of competing with Netflix. Without Net Neutrality, Comcast can slow down Netflix and charge consumers to speed it back up.

The ruling was terrible, but it was made possible by a chain of events set in motion years before. In order to really understand why this is happening, we'll need to follow the money.

headline: Here’s Pete Seeger Doing One Of The Songs He Loved So Much
lede:
I saw Pete Seeger in Seattle about 15 years ago, with Ani DiFranco and several other musicians; they did a version of “We Shall Overcome” that absolutely stunned the entire concert hall, with everybody holding hands and singing along in one of those powerful and electric moments that can happen when humans connect over music.

This clip is from the 2009 inauguration ceremony of newly-elected President Obama. Pete Seeger came to play a little music with Bruce Springsteen, Seeger’s grandson Tao, and many others. Originally written by Woody Guthrie, who Seeger performed with many times, it’s a powerful version of “This Land Is Your Land,” with lyrics (including the frequently-forgotten last few stanzas!) below the video. As always, Pete tried to get the crowd to sing along, shouting out the lyrics so they could all join in.

We’ll miss you, Pete.

headline: Being A Sex Object Is Empowering. Oh, Wait, No It’s Not. Here’s Why.
lede:
Any time we share content that focuses on the ways in which women are objectified or held to absurd physical standards, we hear from some people that say it's just the way it is, that it's been this way for decades, and we should learn to ignore it.

I disagree. Caroline Heldman, the speaker in this video, does an incredible job explaining the objectification of women, how it's gotten worse, how damaging it is, and what we can do to address it.

The seven-step test she walks through is compelling. She begins talking about how we can start fixing the problem at 9:05. Seems so simple... and yet I'm not sure we think of these things regularly. At 11:00, she begins sharing success stories — instances when people who'd had enough decided to take action and made a difference.

This video is for women and men. We should all expect better.

headline: A Funny Commercial That Actually Respects Women! Oh, Except The Tagline At The End.
lede:
Snickers, the chocolate bar, have released a commercial that somehow manages to be crappy and sexist to both men *and* women.

Don't get me wrong, most of the commercial is great. Pretty funny, actually. But then the ending just made me shout at my laptop, "BOOOOO IT WOULD HAVE BEEN PERFECT IF YOU DIDN'T HAVE THAT TAGLINE." It basically reads: treat women with respect? Nah, just eat Snickers and your normal misogynistic self will return! What's even worse is that they make a sweeping generalization that all construction workers are cat-callers. If not eating Snickers means people turn respectful and articulate, this is a terrible advert to get people to go and buy it.

But *perhaps* I'm looking at this too deeply. In short: Catcalling isn't cool. Even yelling "nice" stuff to women randomly on the street isn't cool. But let's face it, Snickers isn't going to solve it, so while the ending of this commercial kinda sucks, I still think the most part of it can be enjoyed.

headline: Being A Dad Of A Daughter Is Hard Enough Without The Dumb Caveman Voices Screaming Inside His Head
lede:
DISCLOSURE: I have a daughter. Someday, she will grow up and become a young woman , and probably want to date people. There's this awful lizard part of my brain that gets protective of her and imagines threatening others who might date her someday, 13 years from now. And while I get protective of my son too, I think differently about each. And it's totally a hypocritical and ridiculous double standard. Because if you raise your kids right, they'll make mistakes, but they'll be responsible and make good choices (hopefully.) Their gender is irrelevant to that. So I want to acknowledge that I'm aware of my rampant hypocrisy. I'm a dad. I'm a jackass. I'm learning how to fight it and hold myself to a higher standard.

Which brings me to Jesse Parent, a dad who says all the things that probably every parent has dealt with thinking all their lives. At 1:50, he disables his lizard brain. And at 2:42, he makes up for his first 2 minutes. Hilariously.

lede:
A few definitions to tee this up:

Oligarchy: A society where power is in the hands of very few people, usually determined by wealth, corporate and family ties, and the military.

The Gilded Age: From the 1870s to the 1900s, our country was very much run by very few people (think John D. Rockefeller, J.P. Morgan, Andrew W. Mellon, Andrew Carnegie) but also marked by extreme poverty. The term was coined by Mark Twain and Charles Dudley Warner to mean, "an era of serious social problems disguised by thin gold gilding."

So ... are we there yet?!

headline: Some Folks Want To Keep A Bit Of History Intact And They Could Really Used A Hand Right Now
lede:
During World War II, women entered the blue collar workforce in huge numbers all over the country. One such place was the Willow Run factory in Michigan where the woman who eventually became “Rosie The Riveter” worked.

That factory us about to be torn down, but there’s a group of people working frantically to try to purchase a small part of the plant and turn it into a museum. They’ve raised 85% of what they need, but with just one day left, there’s a chance they won’t get there. Check the video out and then below that, I’ll tell you how you can help.

headline: Usually, Art Is All About Those In Power. Not For One Amazing Painter.
lede:
Ralph Fasanella was born on Labor Day, 1914. He was the son of an Italian immigrant, and one of his first jobs was slinging ice back in the days when "icebox" meant refrigerator ... with a block of ice. He went on to work in a factory and as a truck driver, and then became a union organizer.

That was before he became a fascinating painter. He often used large canvasses, because he envisioned his work to be in union halls, rather than, as he said, “to hang in some rich guy’s living room.” Some of his paintings were about common working people; others, about strikes, civil unrest, JFK's assasination, and other relics of the times.

His works are on display right now at the Smithsonian American Art Museum in Washington, DC, and a parallel exhibit is also happening in the lobby of the AFL-CIO building. More on that below the images.

headline: A Law Professor's Brilliant Plan Turns The Tables On Corrupt Politicians
lede:
How bad has the money in politics situation gotten? A new study by researchers at Princeton and Northwestern found that, and I'm quoting directly here: "When the preferences of economic elites and the stands of organized interest groups are controlled for, the preferences of the average American appear to have only a minuscule, near-zero, statistically non-significant impact upon public policy.”

In other words: If you can't afford to hire a lobbyist or raise money for politicians, your opinion literally does not matter.

But don't go into a hopeless despair spiral just yet. On May 1st, Harvard Law professor Lawrence Lessig launched Mayday PAC: A crowdfunded Super PAC with the sole mission of forcing Congress to get money out of politics. The response so far has been overwhelming: They've raised over half a million dollars in the first week alone.

headline: How Many People Do You Know Who Are Not 100% Straight Or Gay? More Then You Think.
lede: Sexuality is a gigantic spectrum of endless possibilities and get this, we can choose different ways to express our sexuality based on our sexual orientation. When I was growing up I always thought people were either "gay" or "straight" and never realized there was actually thousands of ways to express sexuality. When we put people in boxes we miss out on all the wonderfully diverse ways that human sexuality can change and all the different ways people of any gender or sex can be compatible with one another. The possibility of combinations is endless, and this photographer thinks it's high time we all came clean about that.

headline: Airbrushing? These Real Women Are Celebrating Their Real Bodies
lede:
After giving birth to her son Sequoia, Jade Baell posted photos of her post-birth body to show the world what a real mother's body looks like.

What happened next was remarkable.

The photo went viral, and something struck Jade: she realised mothers across the world so rarely see themselves reflected accurately in the media. She was flooded with hundreds and thousands of messages from women telling their story about their bodies, how they struggled with not fitting the norm of 'beautiful' and how they felt her photo helped redefine beauty.

Jade proceeded to photograph hundreds of mothers who used to feel 'too saggy', 'too wrinkly' 'too fat', but who now are being celebrated for who they are by Jade and her project. Watch her video below to hear more.

headline: How Much Do You Think About Eating? Not The Food Part. The Food-From-Plate-To-Face Part.
lede: What if three times a day, just like clockwork, you felt overwhelmingly embarrassed and frustrated? If you're living with Parkinson's disease or another disorder that causes hand tremors, it's not a hypothetical. It's the daily experience of eating. Shaky hands make it nearly impossible to get food from plate to mouth without spilling - often on yourself. Able-bodied people like me don't have to think twice before picking up a knife and fork in front of people. So I'm glad to know inventions like this will make it easier for people with tremors to live happier lives with less effort and more dignity while we wait for a cure.

lede:

As he got older, he came to realize he was struggling with the fact that his gender identity didn't match his gender and began the long transition to becoming a man. This is his story.

headline: In The Last 33 Years, 70 Of The 71 Mass-Murderers In The U.S. All Had 1 Thing In Common
lede:
They were all men. Beyond that, most of them felt they were somehow being denied something that they should have been given. That attitude didn't appear out of thin air. It was honed by our culture, generation after generation, perpetuating bad ideas and stereotypes over time. Elliot Rodger is just the latest permutation of the guy who thinks that he is owed something and demands retribution. Rather that figure out that maybe he might not be communicating with women properly, he blamed their lack of interest on them.

The vast majority of men aren't evil, though. It does us no good to vilify an entire gender. Our culture that perpetuates it, on the other hand, needs to be scrutinized.

headline: In The Last 33 Years, 70 Of The 71 Mass-Murderers In The U.S. All Had 1 Thing In Common
lede:
They were all men. Beyond that, most of them felt they were somehow being denied something that they should have been given. That attitude didn't appear out of thin air. It was honed by our culture, generation after generation, perpetuating bad ideas and stereotypes over time. Elliot Rodger is just the latest permutation of the guy who thinks that he is owed something and demands retribution. Rather that figure out that maybe he might not be communicating with women properly, he blamed their lack of interest on them.

The vast majority of men aren't evil, though. It does us no good to vilify an entire gender. Our culture that perpetuates it, on the other hand, needs to be scrutinized.

headline: A Funny Commercial That Actually Respects Women! Oh, Except The Tagline At The End.
lede:
Snickers, the chocolate bar, have released a commercial that somehow manages to be crappy and sexist to both men *and* women.

Don't get me wrong, most of the commercial is great. Pretty funny, actually. But then the ending just made me shout at my laptop, "BOOOOO IT WOULD HAVE BEEN PERFECT IF YOU DIDN'T HAVE THAT TAGLINE." It basically reads: treat women with respect? Nah, just eat Snickers and your normal misogynistic self will return! What's even worse is that they make a sweeping generalization that all construction workers are cat-callers. If not eating Snickers means people turn respectful and articulate, this is a terrible advert to get people to go and buy it.

But *perhaps* I'm looking at this too deeply. In short: Catcalling isn't cool. Even yelling "nice" stuff to women randomly on the street isn't cool. But let's face it, Snickers isn't going to solve it, so while the ending of this commercial kinda sucks, I still think the most part of it can be enjoyed.

lede:
One very mentally ill young man who blamed women for his failure to actually get dates and get along with women killed 6 people and wounded 7 more. The Internet responded in a huge way, and it's still actually doing so right now. The hashtag #YesAllWomen was born, and it absolutely took Twitter by storm; millions of Tweets have gone out with that hashtag.

lede:

headline: A Guy Killed Some People Because He Couldn’t Get A Date, And Twitter Responded In A Massive Way.
lede:
One very mentally ill young man who blamed women for his failure to actually get dates and get along with women killed 6 people and wounded 7 more. The Internet responded in a huge way, and it's still actually doing so right now. The hashtag #YesAllWomen was born, and it absolutely took Twitter by storm; millions of Tweets have gone out with that hashtag.

I have read literally hundreds of them if not more, and I can tell you they are chilling. When I mentioned the hashtag and some of the stories to my wife, she replied, "Of course...I always carry my keys in a way that they can be used if someone attacks me. We learn that early on." For someone who considers himself a pretty well educated and in-touch dude, it rather floored me.

Here is a map of the Tweets from around the world, and two of my favorite Tweets, but there are so many more of these conversations happening right now on Twitter; link to get there is below.

headline: A Great Way To Piss Off Those Who Think It's Okay To Harass Women In The Street
lede:
Every day women are harassed in the street simply by being a woman. Or in other words: every time we step out the house we run the risk of being shouted at, cat-called or assaulted usually in broad daylight. FUN!

Brooklyn based artist Tatyana Fazlalizadeh wanted to take women's voices and faces and plaster them big and bold in the very same places where this takes place. She's addressing gender based street harassment by taking a place where women feel uncomfortable and turning it into a place where we cannot be ignored through street art, and that is pretty awesome.

headline: A Councilman Spectacularly Reverses His Anti-LGBT Bill After A Transgender Woman Quotes The Bible
lede:
In late 2014, a city council in America passed a LGBT non-discrimination ordinance by a 6-to-1 vote, banning discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity. Yay, progress! But who was the one sole person who opposed it? Conservative councilman Ron Webb, who said that he opposes the non-discrimination law because "The Bible tells you homosexuals are an abomination."

Webb drafted a resolution to repeal it — so the community got together a city council meeting to discuss the repeal measure.

Enter the awesome Pamela Raintree, a transgender woman who stood up with a stone and used her own bible passage to call Webb out on his actions. Minutes later after hearing her words, Webb withdrew his resolution without calling for a vote. Hear the incredible thing she had to say below.

headline: An Argument About Your Privacy That Is So Simple, A Little Kid Can Make It
lede:
Our right to a free and open Internets has been under threat lately. The NSA — btw, that stands for the National Security Agency, which has the fancy responsibility of analyzing and acting upon security data — has gotten into the habit of spying on Americans with no justification (including 12 spies who were using NSA tools to spy on their significant others). No, I'm not kidding.

The FCC — btw, that stands for the Federal Communications Commission, which is supposed to regulate and protect our communications channels — just made it easier for big companies to control the speed at which you are allowed to access particular websites. For example, your Internet company (i.e., Comcast or Verizon) could turn into a tiered pay system. So instead of being like a public utility where everyone gets the same amount of water or electricity, Verizon could give Netflix faster access for a fee, but then the smaller start-up that wants to compete and couldn't afford it would get slower access.

The Internet has become one of the most important resources in our lives. It's a shared resource that all of us take part in. Government spying on it, and corporate interference in it are probably not things we want for the future. So Mozilla had some children voice concern for their own future. Because it's kind of important. What kind of web do you want?

headline: Stephen Colbert Calls Out Cable News On Their Inability To Report Actual News
lede:
Being a 24 hour news station is hard. You have find ways to fill 24 hours of airtime without being redundant and without there being breaking news every single day. For CNN, it's even tougher, because their bosses don't actually care about news quality, they care about ratings. They generally just let shrill politically partisan people scream past each other for half the day without fact checking them, and the other half, they underfund their actual reporters and do no long term investigative journalism. Instead, they find something sensationalist to milk and hype until it's been beaten to death with the tedious cudgel that is Wolf Blitzer's beard of indifference.

Stephen Colbert decided to get to the bottom of their latest non-story, the story of if there was any story left about the tragedy on the crash of a Malaysian Airlines plane. He nails it.

They generally just let shrill politically partisan people scream past each other for half the day without fact checking them, and the other half, they underfund their actual reporters and do no long term investigative journalism. Instead, they find something sensationalist to milk and hype until it's been beaten to death with the tedious cudgel that is Wolf Blitzer's beard of indifference.

The Internet responded in a huge way, and it's still actually doing so right now. The hashtag #YesAllWomen was born, and it absolutely took Twitter by storm; millions of Tweets have gone out with that hashtag.

When I mentioned the hashtag and some of the stories to my wife, she replied, "Of course...I always carry my keys in a way that they can be used if someone attacks me. We learn that early on." For someone who considers himself a pretty well educated and in-touch dude, it rather floored me.

headline: When A Black Actor Can't 'Act Black', What Does He Do?
lede:

headline: A Caveman Turns Into A Feminist In Less Than 3 Minutes
lede:
DISCLOSURE: I have a daughter. Someday, she will grow up and become a young woman , and probably want to date people. There's this awful lizard part of my brain that gets protective of her and imagines threatening others who might date her someday, 13 years from now. And while I get protective of my son too, I think differently about each. And it's totally a hypocritical and ridiculous double standard. Because if you raise your kids right, they'll make mistakes, but they'll be responsible and make good choices (hopefully.) Their gender is irrelevant to that. headline: You Know The Stereotypes About Old, Conservative, White Guys? Yea, Don't Judge A Book By It's Cover.
lede:

He finally let everyone know that his Grandparents came to this country legally, but they brought him here at age 5 and he never had gotten proper legal status. So he lived undocumented for most of his life. Jose came out in the national news and then decided to make a documentary about his journey and his fight to get rational immigration reform on the books in the United States.

That's when he met a self proclaimed "hardcore Republican" farmer named Lawrence. Lawrence has a far different perspective than much of his party when it comes to immigration. Here's why.

headline: Here's What Morgan Freeman Had To Say About Racism And Here's A Guy Explaining What He Got Wrong

headline: A Transgender Woman Dares Councilman To Stone Her After He Tried To Introduce Discriminatory Law
lede:
In late 2014, a city council in America passed a LGBT non-discrimination ordinance by a 6-to-1 vote, banning discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity. Yay, progress! But who was the one sole person who opposed it? Conservative councilman Ron Webb, who said that he opposes the non-discrimination law because "The Bible tells you homosexuals are an abomination."

Webb drafted a resolution to repeal it — so the community got together a city council meeting to discuss the repeal measure.

Enter the awesome Pamela Raintree, a transgender woman who stood up with a stone and used her own bible passage to call Webb out on his actions. Minutes later after hearing her words, Webb withdrew his resolution without calling for a vote. Hear the incredible thing she had to say below.

headline: Stephen Colbert Calls Out Cable News On Their Inability To Report Actual News
lede:
Being a 24 hour news station is hard. You have find ways to fill 24 hours of airtime without being redundant and without there being breaking news every single day. For CNN, it's even tougher, because their bosses don't actually care about news quality, they care about ratings. They generally just let shrill politically partisan people scream past each other for half the day without fact checking them, and the other half, they underfund their actual reporters and do no long term investigative journalism. Instead, they find something sensationalist to milk and hype until it's been beaten to death with the tedious cudgel that is Wolf Blitzer's beard of indifference.

Stephen Colbert decided to get to the bottom of their latest non-story, the story of if there was any story left about the tragedy on the crash of a Malaysian Airlines plane. He nails it.
